answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashing stake before it can claim rewards or vote. The trellis of contracts links each claim to that deposit, while a lantern-style audit samples behavior and lets challengers prove copied or coordinated submissions; confirmed abuse burns the stake. Sybils are still possible, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it, so multiplying identities is costly rather than free. An oasis of low-cost entry can remain for untrusted agents, but their influence stays limited until they build a costly record.
